data.name: Charan
data.gender_notes: Charan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Charan is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Chara’ which means ‘to move, to roam, or to go.’ This name is associated with the divine feet of the gods and signifies taking the first steps on a spiritual or physical journey. In Hindu mythology, the divine feet of gods are considered sacred and auspicious. The name Charan carries the meaning “Footstep, path, journey” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Charan usually hope their child will grow to embody footstep, path, journey and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Steps towards spiritual growth and enlightenment
data.etymology: Charan belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Footstep, path, journey.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Charan total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: Krishna is one of the most widely revered and beloved deities in the Hindu tradition. He is believed to be the eighth avatar (or incarnation) of the god Vishnu, and is central to the Hindu epics Mahabharata and Bhagavad Gita.
data.spiritual_significance: Krishna represents the divine playmaker whose playful leela inspires devotion by serving as a reminder of the divine and the ultimate goal of self-realization. He is also considered a symbol of love, compassion, and protectorship.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Charan means the feet, considered as sacred in Hinduism. It symbolizes the journey of the soul from the material world to the divine, as the feet are the first to touch the sacred ground at a temple or holy site. The name Charan is a reminder of the importance of staying grounded and connected to the spiritual path during life's journey.

historical_references.reference: Charan is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Chara' meaning 'to move'. In Hindu mythology, Charan is a title given to revered saints and gods, denoting their ability to move freely between the material and spiritual worlds.
historical_references.context: Hindu mythology, revered saints and gods

historical_references.reference: Charan was also the name of a legendary king of the Satavahana dynasty in ancient India, who ruled around 110 CE. He is known for his military prowess and his patronage of art and culture.
historical_references.context: Ancient India, Satavahana dynasty, legendary king

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Charan, which means 'feet' in Sanskrit, is seen as a symbol of reverence and devotion in Hinduism. On Instagram, there are several accounts dedicated to Charanamrita (the holy water of the feet), where followers post pictures and stories of their own Charanamrita experiences. On YouTube, there are videos of Charanamrita Pooja (worship of the feet) and Charan Sparsh (touching the feet of elders and gurus as a sign of respect). Additionally, meditation apps often incorporate Charanamrita practices, such as visualizing the divine feet in front of you and offering respects, to promote mindfulness and spiritual growth.
